reason: Mechanically it can be built byte-identical-when-off and fail-soft: with env default 0 it skips everything, and on an exception pp={} leaves the cost unchanged. It still fails the schedule and value lens. (1) Slots: 26 Sep is fully booked in the v3 plan (S2 K2, S3->K3b, S4 K3, S5 K3b, S6 K4). The first free slot is 27 Sep S7-S11, which must be submitted before 12:00 under R8, and its score arrives ~19:00-22:00 27 Sep, on a base (K2 or K3) that is not known until the 26 Sep scores. Stacking it with K3/K3b/K4 at the 28 Sep 12:00 consolidation would be untested. (2) Gate: the booster was trained on train GT, so the exp60 lab is in-sample and the only pre-LB check is a dummy that shows it runs. This has the same shape as the closed edge filter (in-sample learned edge prior, +0.016 local, 0 on LB). pair_ship.py's own evidence comes from arm A, which it says 'IS NOT THE CHAMPION' (no gap-close or safe-div); it gives a sign and size only. (3) Rules: relink feeds readmit, so the node set moves and R4 applies (Delta >= +0.002 to enter F1). The idea's own expected gain is +0 to +0.0015, so P(adoption) is ~10%, and a +0.001 result does not change the finals because F2 = exp52. (4) Port risk: the recipe targets Corwin's cell_06 with ONE relink call. x138 calls motion_relink_edges twice (pass 1 -> readmit_discarded_detections -> pass 2, joined notebook source l.3627-3632), so readmitted nodes need a second seed pass and a second feature/score pass. That is 2 extra relink passes plus 2 scoring passes per clip, a variant pair_ship says was never measured. (5) Runtime: the '~4 h headroom' is measured against the 12 h Kaggle limit, not against K2's internal gates. step0.md gives K2 ~7.8 h worst case against the 28,800 s insertion gate, a margin of ~0.2 h, about 7 s/clip over N~100. On 4 vCPU (Corwin measured 0.44 s/film seed on 32 vCPU), x138's flow-seed Hungarian relink run twice more, plus flow_at's per-node Python loop and LightGBM on ~1M pairs, can exceed 7 s/clip. In the worst-case world the fail-soft insertion is then skipped on the last clips, so it confounds the probe and costs the insertion gain unless the gate is moved, which means rebuilding and re-dummying FD/FF. (6) The booster is not yet local (only the .names.json was pulled). It needs the Kaggle dataset attached with the sha pinned, and lightgbm availability in the pinned image is unverified. (7) R10: it is not on the agent-hours priority list, and 4-6 h on 26 Sep competes with exp60 analysis and the K3/K3b/K4 builds.
fix: Do not schedule it in the v3 plan. Keep it only as a conditional 27 Sep spare-slot rider under all of these conditions: (a) RE-AIM and every planned K3/K3b/K4 slot has resolved and a 27 Sep slot is genuinely unused; (b) the agent has <= 3 h to spend after the R10 items are done; (c) it is built on the then-current F1 candidate with PAIR_SCORER default 0, a try/except that falls back to pp={}, and the booster sha pinned from the attached dataset corwin1979/biocel-aux-4d9e2c17; (d) the dummy log records per-clip pair+extra-relink seconds and the build ships only if the extra cost is <= 5 s/clip, or its dummy also re-runs FD/FF with the insertion gate kept at 8.0 h; (e) the pre-readmit node-count identity check passes; (f) one coefficient (16), no ladder, a pre-registered R4 threshold of +0.002, and it is dropped on anything less.
realistic_gain: Expected value ~+0.0002 on the final pick: P(Delta>=+0.002 on public) ~0.1, times ~+0.002, minus the risk that the insertion gate is hit in the worst-case runtime world. Most likely outcome: 0 or +0.001 on public, which R4 does not admit to F1, at the cost of one LB slot and 4-6 agent hours.
